points.description: States the core fact: the compiler copies (inserts/expands) the function's code at each place the function is called, rather than making a jump/call to a single shared copy.
points.partial_credit: Half credit for saying the code is substituted or expanded at the call site without making clear it is a copy at every call, or saying it is copied without naming the call sites.

points.description: States the second detail: this copying happens at every place where a function call is made (each call site), so the code appears once per call.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the idea that the compiler copies the function body into each call site, rather than calling one shared copy. Award part marks (P1) for a vague statement such as "the code is inserted where it is called" with no sense of copying. Give no marks for answers that only describe inline as a keyword or as a request, or that describe a single shared function body or a jump to one copy.
